overall_quality.reason: Accurate, concise explanation of compiler vs interpreter distinction with reasonable tradeoffs, though lacks examples or mention of hybrid approaches (e.g., JIT).
overall_quality.evidence: A compiler and an interpreter both translate source code into machine code, but they do so in different ways. A compiler translates the entire program into machine code before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes the code line by line. This means a compiler is faster for large programs, but an interpreter is more flexible and can adapt to changes in the code during execution.
